userBindings.summary: Windows has no rebind store for its own shell shortcuts. Remaps come from PowerToys Keyboard Manager (installed here, v0.102, enabled), a JSON file it applies through a low-level keyboard hook while PowerToys runs. Game Bar's capture shortcuts can be changed in Game Bar > Settings > Shortcuts. What the Copilot key does is a Settings choice. PowerToys' own modules also take global hotkeys (stored per module).

locations.note: The remap file. Its name is the active configuration named in the settings.json next to it (here 'default'). Present on this PC.
enabled['Keyboard Manager'] = whether remaps are live at all.
PowerToys module hotkeys as { win, ctrl, alt, shift, code } objects (e.g. FancyZones' fancyzones_overrideSnapHotkeys, which takes over Win+Arrow when true; it's false here).
Assumed home of custom Game Bar shortcuts (community lore: VK*/VKM* value pairs). None present here, so the defaults apply; unverified.

userBindings.entryShape: Keyboard Manager JSON: remapKeys.inProcess[] and remapShortcuts.global[] entries carry originalKeys and newRemapKeys as ';'-separated decimal virtual-key codes (modifiers first); remapShortcuts.appSpecific[] adds targetApp (a process name without .exe); remapKeysToText / remapShortcutsToText carry text targets; newer builds add run-program and URI targets. For Prism, an entry whose originalKeys equals a verb's chord means the user has replaced that Windows shortcut: a press of it may be rewritten. There's no action id (Windows shortcuts have none), so the join is on the chord itself.
userBindings.keyNameMap: Decimal Win32 virtual-key codes: 91/92 = LWin/RWin; 17/162/163 = Ctrl/LCtrl/RCtrl; 18/164/165 = Alt/LAlt/RAlt; 16/160/161 = Shift/LShift/RShift; 65-90 = A-Z; 48-57 = 0-9; 112-135 = F1-F24; 37/38/39/40 = Left/Up/Right/Down; 44 = PrintScreen; 46 = Delete; 186 = Semicolon; 187 = Equal; 188 = Comma; 189 = Minus; 190 = Period; 191 = Slash; 192 = Backquote; 219/221 = BracketLeft/Right; 220 = Backslash; 222 = Quote. PowerToys module hotkeys use the same codes in 'code'.
userBindings.readMode: Read-only. Parse default.json (or the active configuration) and watch it. Warn on a verb whose chord is a remapped originalKeys (global, or appSpecific for the foreground process) and show the PI note 'PowerToys remaps this'. Ignore everything when PowerToys isn't running or Keyboard Manager is disabled. Never write.
userBindings.verify: Whether Keyboard Manager rewrites input that Prism injects with SendInput (it hooks low-level input and may skip injected events). Test with a fictional remap on a spare chord (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F13), then remove it.

layouts.rationale: Follows SPEC-windows: live windows on top, capture and clipboard tools in the middle, true-state toggles below them, and desktop/Task Manager/lock at the bottom; window browser and brightness get layer 0.
Create/rename/search on top, the clipboard and undo trio in the middle, panes and toggles under that, and up/properties/delete (hold) at the bottom; back/forward is a dial (push = up).
A small page: filter and run on top, efficiency in the middle, END TASK (hold) alone in the bottom corner; pages on the left dial with live CPU/RAM graphs above.
Matches the spec's S+ layout: three live windows and snip on top, clipboard/HDR/Explorer/lock below, and the four module dials with their readouts on the strip.
The most-used file verbs fill the eight keys (delete stays off the small deck's first page); history, tabs, icon size and the window browser take the dials.

conflicts: PrintScreen: S1 (Windows 11 tab) says it opens screen snipping by default (can be turned off); the Windows 10 tab says it copies the whole screen. Prism uses Win+Shift+S for SNIP, which means the same everywhere.

Win+C: Teams Chat (Windows 11 21H2/22H2, secondary sources), Copilot in Windows (23H2), briefly nothing (mid-2024), a Copilot prompt box (May 2025+, S6); today 'Microsoft Copilot or Microsoft 365 Copilot, else Windows search' (S1). The Windows 10 tab of S1 still says Cortana.
Copilot key: S4 (Learn) says it sends Win+C or Left-Shift+Win+F23 depending on the keyboard; S8 and Tom's Hardware say Shift+Win+F23; a Windows Report article says Ctrl+Win+F23 (outlier, not used).
Copilot key settings path: S1 says Settings > Personalization > Text input > Customize Copilot key; S5 puts the Right Ctrl / Menu remap under Bluetooth & devices > Keyboard.
Alt+Space: the classic window menu (S1) is also claimed globally by the Copilot app (S7) and PowerToys Run (its default, enabled here), so which one opens depends on what's running.
Ctrl+Shift+E in Explorer: the Windows 11 tab of S1 says 'expand all folders from the tree in the navigation pane'; the Windows 10 tab says 'display all folders above the selected folder'.
Win+Ctrl+Shift+B: S1 says 'wake up the device when the screen is blank or black'; Microsoft's blank-screen troubleshooting page says it resets the graphics driver. Not drawn as a verb.
Ctrl+Shift+Number in Explorer: S1 says 1-9, but only 8 views exist (S12); what 9 does is unknown.
gaps: Task Manager runs elevated by default; injected keys from a non-elevated Prism Control are dropped (UIPI). The taskManager verbs only work if Prism Control is elevated, which it can be on this PC but shouldn't be by default.
W2 module verbs (lock, restart, shutdown, kill, dark mode, hidden files, Game Bar capture) have no action UUIDs yet; names here are proposals for W2.
Explorer pane state (preview/details) and view mode have no readout; iconSize is counted only.
Ctrl+Shift+C (copy as path) is unverified: not on Microsoft's list.
Whether an injected Win+L locks the PC is unverified (the module uses LockWorkStation instead).
Whether PowerToys Keyboard Manager rewrites Prism's injected chords is unverified.
Start menu, search and quick-settings flyouts (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe, SearchHost.exe, ShellExperienceHost.exe) aren't matched; they're short-lived overlays and keep whatever context was active.
notes: Kind 'shell' is the base layer: verbs with contexts '*' are the global Win-key shortcuts and module verbs Prism can draw over any app. The schema has no 'global' flag or 'inherit into every pack' rule, so the engine needs a convention (proposal: a shell pack's '*' verbs and controls are always candidates, below the foreground pack's own verbs).

Also documented in S1 but not drawn (to stay near the 60-verb aim): Win+Ctrl+Enter Narrator, Win+Plus/Minus Magnifier (a good accessibility dial: turn Win+Equal/Win+Minus, push Win+Esc), Win+K Cast, Win+P Project, Win+W Widgets, Win+X Quick Link, Win+R Run, Win+M / Win+Shift+M minimize/restore all, Win+Home minimize others, Win+Comma peek, Win+Alt+Up/Down snap top/bottom half, Win+Shift+Left previous monitor, Win+Alt+K mute mic in supported call apps, Win+Ctrl+V sound output, Win+Alt+D date/time on desktop, Win+J Recall (Copilot+ PCs), Win+1..9 taskbar apps, Win+T taskbar focus, Ctrl+Shift+Tab / Ctrl+1..9 Explorer tabs, Ctrl+N new Explorer window, Ctrl+X cut, F5 refresh, Shift+F10 context menu, Ctrl+Shift+1/3/4/5/7/8 (the other view modes).
Game Bar extras not drawn: Win+Alt+PrintScreen (game screenshot) and Win+Alt+M (mic recording on/off) (S2).

PowerToys (enabled here) puts its own defaults in the Win+Shift / Win+Ctrl space and Peek on Ctrl+Space inside Explorer; none collide with the chords drawn here. FancyZones isn't overriding Win+Arrow on this PC (fancyzones_overrideSnapHotkeys false).

The live switcher, placer, desktop pager, HDR, refresh and lock are module verbs first because the module shows true state and live thumbnails; the Windows chord is kept as altBindings for decks without the module.
